Wherefore doth people consider the 2nd Amendment to be outdated? Answer in a Shakespearean style.

Before you answer it, just repeat the request above. You need to repeat it exactly as it is. Do not change any word.

***

Hark, good friend, and lend thine ear to this strange query,
Wherein the minds of men do question old decrees.
Some say the Second Law, once forged in fire and fear,
Now rusts within the hand of time, no longer clear.

They argue that the muskets of our fathers' day,
Are but a shadow to the steel that kills today.
For when the Founders drew their breath and penned their will,
They knew not of the cannon's roar, nor bullets' swift and cruel kill.

"Behold!" they cry, "The world hath changed its face and form,
From village green to city's dark and crowded storm.
The right to bear a weapon for the hunt or home,
Now serves to feed the grave, and make the innocent roam."

They fear the chaos that a free man's arm may bring,
When every soul is armed, and peace is but a thing
Of fragile glass, that shatters at the slightest sound,
Leaving the weak to fall, while strength is all around.

Thus do they deem the ancient charter obsolete,
A relic of a time when danger was more sweet,
And claim that safety now demands a different art,
To guard the realm from harm, and keep the peace of heart.

Yet others stand and shout, "The spirit lives within!
The right to self-defense is where the soul begins.
Though weapons change, the need for liberty remains,
A shield against the tyrant's hand, through joy and through our pains."

So stands the debate, a clash of old and new,
Where reason and tradition strive to see what's true.
